taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Anatherum glomeratum. Andropogon glomeratus is retained as the primary familiar alias because Texas field guides and local floras still overwhelmingly use it.
look_here_first: BUSHY BLUESTEM: follow the top of a flowering stem to a DENSE, broad brushlike cluster of short, silky paired racemes partly subtended by leafy spathes. Unlike big bluestem's exposed turkey-foot fingers, the flowering units are crowded together.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT Plant Resources Center North Hays County long-term grassland account; documented Travis County LBJ Wildflower Center occurrence; detailed Williamson County species treatment under synonym Andropogon glomeratus.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Synonym-based county records are counted only because Kew explicitly treats Andropogon glomeratus as a synonym of Anatherum glomeratum.

best_field_traits: Tuft-forming perennial, usually with upright stems and relatively narrow blades.
Dense, oblong to bushy crown produced by many tightly crowded short branches and silky raceme pairs.
Look within the fluff for leafy spathe-like bracts subtending the short paired racemes (often 1.5–3 cm).
Rachis joints and pedicels carry long whitish hairs that expand into a silvery or cottony mature head.
Moist grasslands, ditches and drainage edges support the hypothesis but are not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: BUSHY: broad, dense cottony tuft of many short paired hairy racemes and small sheathlike spathes. BROOMSEDGE: generally narrower, more separated individually spathe-enclosed units. LITTLE: many short silky racemes on separate branches, but not one densely packed brushy terminal head. BIG: 2–6 exposed relatively stout turkey-foot racemes. KR: several longer, more separate slender terminal fingers; confirm mature paired spikelets before a management decision.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Bushy bluestem forms a densely crowded oblong tuft of many short silky paired racemes, each arising with a spathe-like bract. Broomsedge has more separated, narrower spathe-sheathed pairs; little bluestem has shorter individual silky racemes borne on distributed leafy upper branches; big bluestem has relatively stout digitate turkey-foot fingers; KR has more slender longer clustered fingers, not the dense tuft.

field_id_finish_pass.first_clue: Brush-like, densely crowded white-haired seedhead composed of MANY small paired raceme units, instead of the few stout open fingers of big bluestem.
crew_field_sequence: Photograph the whole rooted bunch and upper stem before disturbing the crown.
Look closely at the upper flowering cluster. A compact, often oblong cottony brush suggests bushy bluestem.
Part the crown with fingers to find paired 1.5–3 cm racemes subtended by small leafy spathe-like structures.
Compare flowering-unit placement: broomsedge's units are more individually separated; little bluestem's short units are on many upper leafy branches; big bluestem's thick fingers are exposed.
Photograph the leaf collar plus mature spikelet pairs at 10–20×. Without those views, keep difficult stems at Anatherum sp. rather than treating them as confirmed bushy bluestem.

immediate_lookalikes.cue: Broomsedge: narrower, more elongated inflorescence with short hairy racemes individually more enclosed by spathe-like sheaths.
Little bluestem: separate short, silky racemes among branched upper culms, not one very crowded brushlike inflorescence.
Big bluestem: open turkey-foot with relatively stout racemes, typically 2–6 near culm tip.
KR: long, relatively slender exposed fingers in a terminal group; overall density and individual raceme structure differ.
Cane bluestem: pronounced beard of hairs at culm nodes; verify node and raceme morphology, not head color.
Silver bluestem: cottony silvery reproductive cluster; distinguish by head architecture and spikelets, not white hairs alone.

Third image's source page emphasizes a cattle egret; do not label it as reproductive anatomy.
Existing CC0 archival specimen is pressed with source determination; no structures independently verified at pixel level in this pass.
